summary: Tolperisone is a centrally acting muscle relaxant used to treat spasticity following stroke in adults (its EU-authorised indication after restriction) and, in some countries, painful muscle spasm. It is non-sedating relative to other muscle relaxants but its main safety concern is hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. It is not FDA-approved.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of spasticity in adults following stroke (EU-restricted indication)
Treatment of painful muscle spasm associated with musculoskeletal disorders (where locally approved)

dosage.d: 50 mg three times daily, titrated up to 150 mg three times daily according to response
dosage.n: Usual range 150-450 mg/day; use the lowest effective dose

dosage.d: Use with caution; individualise and titrate slowly
dosage.n: Avoid in severe renal or hepatic impairment

admin: Take after meals with a glass of water
Titrate the dose gradually to the lowest effective level
Stop immediately and seek care if a hypersensitivity reaction occurs
moa: Tolperisone is a centrally acting muscle relaxant that stabilises neuronal membranes by blocking voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the central nervous system, particularly in the brainstem, spinal cord, and reticular formation. This reduces reflex and pathologically increased muscle tone without significant sedation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to tolperisone, eperisone, or any excipient

preg: There are insufficient data on use in pregnancy. Avoid, particularly during the first trimester, unless clearly necessary.
lact: Excretion in human milk is not established; breastfeeding is contraindicated during treatment.
renal: Use with caution in moderate renal impairment with careful titration; avoid in severe renal impairment because of limited safety data and potential accumulation.
hepatic: Use with caution in moderate hepatic impairment; avoid in severe hepatic impairment.

moderate: CYP2D6 substrates (e.g., thioridazine, tolperisone may increase their levels)
Other centrally acting muscle relaxants (additive effects)
interactions.food: Take after food; food increases bioavailability and improves tolerability
interactions.diagnostics: No specific test interference; investigate any allergic reaction

monitoring: Signs of hypersensitivity, especially early in therapy
counsel: Take after meals with water as directed
Stop the drug and seek urgent care for rash, swelling of face/lips/throat, wheezing, or difficulty breathing
It is usually non-sedating but report dizziness or marked weakness
Tell your doctor if you have a history of allergies
pk: Store below 25 C; protect from moisture and light
pearls: EU use restricted to post-stroke spasticity in adults after a hypersensitivity safety review
Main safety concern is hypersensitivity, including anaphylaxis - counsel patients to recognise it
Relatively non-sedating compared with other centrally acting muscle relaxants
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited; high doses may cause ataxia, tonic-clonic seizures, dyspnoea, and respiratory depression. Management is supportive (airway, breathing, circulation) with symptomatic treatment of seizures; there is no specific antidote.
